html:
Roman emperor from 98 to 117 CE, under whom the empire reached its largest size. He was the first emperor born outside Italy, at Italica near Seville in Spain.

He was a soldier, governing on the Rhine when the old emperor Nerva adopted him in 97 CE. As emperor he won two wars, in 101 to 102 and 105 to 106 CE, against Decebalus, king of Dacia (roughly modern Romania). Dacia became a province, and its gold paid for great works in Rome: Trajan's Market, a new forum and Trajan's Column, whose spiral relief tells the story of the wars. He also enlarged Portus and expanded the alimenta, a fund to feed poor children in Italy.

From 114 CE he fought the Parthian Empire, took Armenia and Mesopotamia and reached the Persian Gulf. Revolts broke out behind him, and he died in Cilicia on the way home.

The Senate named him optimus princeps, "the best ruler", and later wished new emperors to be "luckier than Augustus, better than Trajan". His successor Hadrian gave up his eastern conquests.
sum: Roman emperor from 98 to 117 CE, under whom the empire reached its largest size. He was the first emperor born outside Italy, at Italica near Seville in Spain.
